rows.description: A teenager who failed an entrance test decides they are stupid and a burden to the family. One event becomes a verdict on the whole self, especially where marks carry family expectations.
graph_context: next stage: Blame and hiding
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: shame

rows.description: The person blames the teacher, the paper or bad luck, or avoids telling parents and friends. Deflecting shields from pain in the short term and blocks any learning from what happened.
graph_context: previous stage: Shame and global verdict
next stage: Facing family and peers
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: A cousin or teacher watches a teen return after a bad result and hears the family compare them with others. A quiet word that one result is not the person, and an offer to plan next steps, matters.
graph_context: previous stage: Blame and hiding
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: After a failed exam or startup, others offer pity, advice or comparison with cousins. Support that carries no judgment, and just listens, helps the person get back to their feet.
graph_context: next stage: Grieving the lost plan
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: The person mourns the future they had pictured, with sadness, envy of peers and doubts about direction. Allowing this grief, rather than rushing to a positive story, is part of moving on.
graph_context: previous stage: Facing family and peers
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, grief, doubt, envy

rows.description: After the first pain eases, the person asks what was in their control, what was luck and what to change. A fair look at causes, neither self-flagellation nor excuses, turns failure into information.
graph_context: next stage: Small steps back
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: The person tries again at a smaller scale, such as a retake, a side project or a new role, and collects small wins. Confidence returns through action, not by thinking one's way to it.
graph_context: previous stage: Honest review
next stage: Story rewritten
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Years later the failure is remembered as a hard chapter that taught resilience and clarified values. The person can speak of it plainly and can support others facing the same.
graph_context: previous stage: Small steps back
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: A fresh graduate joins a company and sees confident colleagues using unfamiliar terms. The excitement of being hired mixes with the worry that the selection was a mistake.
graph_context: next stage: Overworking to hide gaps
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, excitement
related concepts: imposter feelings

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: The new hire stays late, avoids asking questions and quietly studies at night to catch up. Not asking for help feels safer than exposing ignorance, but it slows learning.
graph_context: previous stage: Arrival and anxiety
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: trust
related concepts: imposter feelings
